A standalone product you must install separately on every VM
A feature limited to Azure Storage accounts only
A replacement for the Azure CLI
questions.explain: Azure Monitor is built into the platform itself and covers metrics, logs, alerts, and dashboards for essentially every resource type.

options: Metrics collected automatically for most resources, with no agent install or configuration required
Metrics that only exist after you write a custom KQL query
Metrics that require a paid add-on to enable
A type of Azure Policy rule
questions.explain: Platform metrics like Percentage CPU or Network In/Out start flowing the moment a resource exists — no setup needed.

questions.q: In Metrics Explorer, what does the aggregation setting control?
options: How a metric's data points are summarized over the chosen time range, such as Average vs. Maximum
Which Azure region the metric is collected from
Whether the metric is stored in Log Analytics
The retention period of the underlying data
questions.explain: The same CPU data can look completely different depending on whether you view it as an Average, Maximum, Minimum, Sum, or Count.

questions.q: A VM's Percentage CPU metric looks fine on Average but is pegged near 100% on Maximum for long stretches. What does this suggest?
options: The VM may be undersized for its workload — real evidence worth revisiting the VM size over
The metric data is corrupted and should be ignored
Averages are always more accurate than maximums
The VM has no CPU metric being collected
questions.explain: Switching to Maximum reveals sustained high-CPU periods that an average can hide — a concrete signal to reconsider VM sizing.

questions.q: Which Azure CLI command retrieves the same Percentage CPU data shown in Metrics Explorer?
options: az monitor metrics list --resource <vm-resource-id> --metric "Percentage CPU" --interval PT1H
az vm show --resource-group <rg> --name <vm>
az monitor log-analytics query
az account show
questions.explain: az monitor metrics list pulls the same metric data the portal's Metrics Explorer displays, useful for scripting a health check.
